properties.so_saved_final_prompt: a vertical Sick Ollie v2 software release poster built around exactly two clearly readable text elements: “Sick Nodes” and “Studio”. “Sick Nodes” is the dominant foreground title, enormous, fully formed, opaque, unobstructed, and immediately readable; nothing crosses through the letters. The title uses bold fluorescent hot-pink paint or solid black typography with a crisp acid-yellow lower-right offset, controlled pink-white glow, tactile edges, and a sweeping underline when appropriate. “Studio” is the only secondary readable text, centered inside a small polished chrome badge with rounded clipped corners and crisp black geometric type. A synthetic feminine muse is shown from behind at a slight three-quarter turn, one cheek barely visible, with short icy-lavender hair, pearl-white chrome shell plates, black mirrored internal mechanics, and a partially exposed mechanical neck and spine. The heavy black title above her casts stretched rainbow thermal shadows that pool into a pale airbrushed field, keeping the composition chic, clean, and slightly uncanny. The surrounding field is unmistakably Sick Ollie: a continuous macro thermal-liquid background with deep black negative space, fluorescent hot pink, electric cyan, cobalt blue, ultraviolet, orange, crimson, and acid yellow; oily marbling, glowing cellular forms, wet lacquer highlights, holographic color separation, analog grain, VHS softness, chromatic misregistration, radiant neon halation, glossy resin, liquid chrome, and controlled dye bleed. The background has no room, horizon, floor, landscape, or literal software interface. The central object remains behind the title and never obstructs either readable text element.
